fn6a.notes: VERIFIED (2026-06-13 corpus analysis, 203 instances): FN6A 1 <actor> at disasm idx 0 = initial camera target at scene start (followed by SETPOS/WALKTO for that actor); FN6A 0 <actor> mid-scene = pan camera to actor immediately before they speak (consistently precedes SAY with matching actor id). Both modes mean 'look at this actor'; mode distinguishes initial-lock vs mid-scene-focus.

fn6b.notes: VERIFIED (2026-06-13 corpus analysis, 90 instances): FN6B 1 x y at disasm idx 0 = snap camera to coords at scene start; FN6B 0 x y mid-scene = move camera to coords. Mode 1 = scene-start snap, mode 0 = mid-scene pan.

waitflag.notes: VERIFIED (2026-06-13 corpus analysis): WAITFLAG releases when gesture animation completes. Preceding SETANIM opcodes are always gesture/action anims (anim 54: 26x, anim 9: 15x, anim 57: 5x, etc.), never idle/walk loops. Pattern: SETANIM <gesture> -> WAITFLAG -> SETANIM <idle>. 48-frame default is reasonable approximation.

emotes.notes: FALSIFIED (2026-06-13): No emote TIM art found in tim/dw2003/field/ tree. Effect actor ids 800-835 are PS1 heap objects; their TIM art is runtime-loaded from the wstag overlay or cmnbgdtm pack by native call 0x80092484 - not a separate sprite directory. Glyph fallback is correct approach.

transitions.notes: All intro transitions are HANDOFF opcodes already followed by the engine (handoff_to). Only the two special ids below need code.

menu_interleave.notes: VERIFIED (2026-06-13 static analysis): SAY p1=14 = strings[13] = 'Have you all decided?' (Account Clerk). Pack+lead menus fire after this SAY via afterSay hook. SAY p1=16 = strings[15] = 'Okay, then I'll register you...' is the last line before HANDOFF 1280. esdmg700[1] has NO choice markup; all 16 strings are linear SAYs. Name entry is at HANDOFF 1280 (disasm idx 294) after ev1 ends, before ev3.

title_art.notes: FOUND but not decoded (2026-06-13): pack/dw2003/screen/tlogousa/ has 13 bin files in sub-pack 0 + 3 in sub-pack 1. Also tlogopal (PAL) and tlogojpn (JPN) variants. These are raw PS1 TIM format; the extraction tool has not processed screen-type packs. No PNG available. Canvas-drawn title screen is correct current approach.

screen_id_correction.notes: IMPORTANT: screen id != stage number. s780 = screen 727, s785 = screen 728, s790 = screen 729. See data/screen_table.json for authoritative mapping. The task brief's claim that 'screen id = hex of stage number' (e.g. 0x30C = s780) is wrong; 0x30C = 780 decimal is a different stage.
